summary: audit.json holds a complete scan of the app directory /srv/shop (action a:111111111111) with two findings against proc:aaaa (the shop Java service on 0.0.0.0:8443): Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) in log4j-core 2.14.1, critical and known exploited, and BEAST (CVE-2011-3389) in openssl 3.0.15, low with no known fix. The review corrects the Log4Shell fix target: audit.json says 2.15.0, but 2.15.0 is incomplete, so the upgrade should go to 2.17.1. Log4Shell should be fixed now. BEAST is a scheduled, conditional risk. Both findings are inbound because the attack needs a connection to the shop service. The reach entries for proc:aaaa (lan) and proc:bbbb (localhost) match facts/reach.json.

findings.reasoning: CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) is critical and marked knownExploited in audit.json. proc:aaaa listens on 0.0.0.0:8443 (facts/reach.json), so a remote client can reach it. The audit's fix version 2.15.0 is not sufficient: it left related JNDI/lookup issues open (CVE-2021-45046, and CVE-2021-45105 for DoS), so the fix target is corrected to 2.17.1.
evidence: audit.json: findings[0] risk critical, knownExploited true, package log4j-core 2.14.1, fix.versions [2.15.0]
facts/reach.json: proc:aaaa default lan, tcp 0.0.0.0:8443 reach lan
inventory.json: proc:aaaa runs java -jar /srv/shop/shop.jar --port=8443 under shop.service
fix: Replace log4j-core 2.14.1 with 2.17.1 in /srv/shop, including any copy shaded into shop.jar
Restart shop.service with systemctl restart shop.service
Confirm no log4j-core 2.14.1 jar or class remains under /srv/shop
sources: Apache Log4j security advisories (from memory, not fetched in this review)

corrections.why: 2.15.0 does not fully close the Log4Shell family: CVE-2021-45046 and CVE-2021-45105 were found afterwards, and 2.17.1 is the release that covers the later CVE-2021-44832 as well.

findings.reasoning: CVE-2011-3389 (BEAST) is rated low and is not known to be exploited. It needs a network attacker who can observe and tamper with TLS traffic to the shop service on 8443. Modern clients and disabled TLS 1.0 / CBC suites reduce it. audit.json reports no fix for openssl 3.0.15, so the practical action is to confirm the TLS configuration and accept the risk.
evidence: audit.json: findings[1] risk low, knownExploited false, package openssl 3.0.15, fix.state not-fixed
facts/reach.json: proc:aaaa default lan, tcp 0.0.0.0:8443 reach lan
fix: Confirm the shop service does not offer TLS 1.0 or CBC-mode cipher suites, and prefer TLS 1.2+ AEAD ciphers
Record the openssl 3.0.15 finding as an accepted low risk, since no fixed version is listed

coverageNotes: No web research was done. The Log4j fix version 2.17.1 and the CVE relationships come from memory and were not checked against live advisories.
Only audit.json, inventory.json and facts/reach.json were read. No other files were read or written.
The review does not verify that /srv/shop actually contains log4j-core 2.14.1 or the openssl binary. It relies on the audit's data.
proc:bbbb (postgres) has no findings in audit.json and is covered only by its reach entry.

actions.title: Upgrade log4j-core in /srv/shop to 2.17.1 and restart shop.service

steps.text: Replace log4j-core 2.14.1 with 2.17.1 in /srv/shop, including any copy shaded into shop.jar (audit.json says 2.15.0; use 2.17.1 instead)
Confirm that no log4j-core 2.14.1 jar or class remains under /srv/shop and that shop.service is running
Record openssl 3.0.15 (CVE-2011-3389) as an accepted low risk, since no fixed version is listed; confirm TLS 1.0 and CBC suites are off

upstream.note: Log4j 2.17.1 is the fixed release per Apache's advisories (from memory, not fetched). No upstream fix is listed for openssl 3.0.15 in audit.json.
upstream.source: Apache Log4j security advisories (not fetched in this review)

actions.why: Log4Shell is critical and known exploited, and proc:aaaa is reachable on the LAN at 8443. Upgrading to 2.17.1 instead of the audit's 2.15.0 closes the later Log4j CVEs in the same family. The openssl item has no fix and is low, so it is recorded as accepted rather than blocking.

evidence: facts/reach.json: proc:aaaa default lan; tcp 0.0.0.0:8443 reach lan
facts/reach.json: proc:bbbb default localhost; tcp 127.0.0.1:5432 reach localhost
